subject: Covariates and predicting counts space-time LGCP

messages.author: 7b72881378080971
messages.subject: Covariates and predicting counts space-time LGCP
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to put together a script to model space-time point process with INLA using LGCP. I would like to use the model to predict counts across space and time but am having trouble with 2 aspects of this. 

1) including a covariate. I'm not sure if the way I have coded this is correct. The model runs, but confirmation from someone that what I have written is correct would be great.
2) converting the intensity surface to counts. As I understand it, the intercept + the random field (plus covariate effects if included) is the log (poisson) intensity, where intensity is expressed as mean count per unit space time. So to get counts per cell you have to exponentiate the log-intensity and multiply it by the space-time volume of the grid cell. When I do this, the space-time intensity surface seems to not line up with the observed counts. 

I've attached some code - this is a modification of the space-time LGCP example in the SPDE manual which uses the Burkitt dataset. I've just created a toy covariate and added some lines to try to estimate counts at the end.

Any comments/thoughts on these two issues would be much appreciated.

Thanks! Hugh

and when computing the 'cellVol' you them considered 'c0' from the temporal mesh
 cellVol<-cellArea*diag(inla.mesh.fem(mesh.t)$c0)[1]

Elias

Hi Hugh,

This is just a scaling, like the scaling you did for time to have it in the [0, 1] interval.  However, you have to use the same time window in both parts of your code in order to make it consistent.

Notice that considering the time knots you have, the first (and the last) element in diagonal of c0 in this case is half of the others.

Elias

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Covariates and predicting counts space-time LGCP
parts:
On 24/03/16 20:43, Hugh Sturrock wrote:
> I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong..??

Previously in the code you computed st.volume as:

st.volume <- diag(kronecker(Diagonal(n=k),
spde$param.inla$M0))

where by having Diagonal(n=k) means that the time window has size equals
1. So, it is different of what you them used to compute the predicted
counts. You do need to use the same widow size in both parts of your code.

Elias
